Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verses 1–2:

Surat al-Taghabun is Madaniyyah (Medinan) [[Ibn al-Duraysi, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Surat al-Taghabun was revealed in Medina. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr who said: Surat al-Taghabun was revealed in Medina. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/181.]] ﷽

* *

'Ata' said: It is Makkiyyah (Meccan) except for three verses, from His saying: "O you who believe, indeed among your spouses and your children..." to its end [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/125. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/181.]].

﴿He glorifies Allah whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent. He is the One who created you, so among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: Indeed Allah created the children of Adam as believers and disbelievers, then He will restore them on the Day of Resurrection just as He created them, believers and disbelievers [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 12/382 (edition of Mahmud Shakir), al-Lalaka'i in Sharh Usul I'tiqad Ahl al-Sunnah: 3/547, and al-Ajurri in al-Shari'ah p. 211.]].

And we have been related from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the boy whom al-Khidr (peace be upon him) killed was sealed as a disbeliever" [[Narrated by Muslim as a marfu' hadith in al-Qadar, chapter on the meaning of "every child is born upon the fitrah," and the ruling on the death of children of disbelievers and children of Muslims, no. (2661): 4/2050.]].

And He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: "And they will not beget except a wicked, ungrateful disbeliever" [Nuh: 27].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 64, verse 3:**

Abu Abdullah... (no, let me translate exactly):

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi related to us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us; Sulayman ibn Harb related to us; Hammad related to us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Anas [from Anas] [[Omitted from "B".]], from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Allah has appointed an angel over the womb. He says: 'O Lord, a drop of semen! O Lord, a clinging clot! O Lord, a lump of flesh!' When Allah wills to complete its creation, he says: 'O Lord, male or female? Wretched or blessed? What is its provision and what is its term?' And so it is written while it is in its mother's belly." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the beginning of the Book of Qadar (11/477), and in the Book of Menstruation, chapter "Formed and Unformed..."; and by Muslim in the Book of Qadar, no. (2646) (4/2038); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (1/127-128).]]

A group said: The meaning of the verse is that Allah created the creatures, and then some of them disbelieved and some believed, because Allah the Exalted mentioned the creation and then described them by their own actions, saying: ﴿Among you is a disbeliever, and among you is a believer﴾, just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah created every creature from water; of them is one that walks on its belly, and of them is one that walks on two legs...﴾ [al-Nur: 45]. Allah created them, and walking is their own act. Then they differed in its interpretation. It was narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that he said: "Among you is a disbeliever" in his life, "a believer" in the end; "and among you is a believer" in his life, "a disbeliever" in the end.

Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: "Among you is a disbeliever in Allah, a believer in the stars; and among you is a believer in Allah, a disbeliever in the stars." [[See al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/276-277.]]

It was also said: ﴿Among you is a disbeliever﴾ in that Allah the Exalted created him, and this is the doctrine of the Dahriyya (materialists who deny the Creator); "and among you is a believer" in that Allah created him. [[See al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/277.]]

The summary of the matter is this: Allah created the disbeliever, and his disbelief is an act of his and an acquisition (kasb) of his; and He created the believer, and his belief is an act of his and an acquisition of his. So each of the two groups has an acquisition and a choice, and their acquisition and choice occur by the decree and will of Allah. Thus the believer, after Allah has created him, chooses belief, because Allah the Exalted willed this from him, decreed it for him, and knew it of him. And the disbeliever, after Allah the Exalted has created him, chooses disbelief, because Allah the Exalted willed this from him, decreed it for him, and knew it of him. This is the path of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community); whoever follows it is correct and is safe from jabr (determinism that denies human agency) and qadar (the error of denying divine decree).

﴿He knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose. And God knows well what is in the breasts.﴾

﴿Has there not come to you﴾ the news (naba') of those who disbelieved before? (This is addressed to the disbelievers of Makkah.) ﴿Meaning the earlier nations.﴾ ﴿So they tasted the evil consequence of their affair﴾, meaning what befell them of punishment in this world. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾ in the Hereafter.

﴿That﴾ punishment is ﴿because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said: "Shall mere human beings guide us?"﴾ He did not say "yahdinā" (guide us), because al-bashar (the human being), although its form is singular, carries the meaning of the plural. It is a collective noun (ism al-jins) with no singular derived from its form; its singular is insān (human). Its meaning: they denied and said, "A mortal like us guides us!" ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away, and God was self-sufficient﴾ regarding their faith, ﴿and God is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy﴾ in His deeds.

Then He informed of their denial of resurrection, so He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿Those who disbelieved claim that they will never be resurrected. Say﴾
﴿Those who disbelieved claim that they will never be resurrected. Say﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿"Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed of what you did. And that is easy for God. So believe in God and His Messenger, and the light which We have sent down"﴾, which is the Qur'an. ﴿And God is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

﴿The Day He gathers you for the Day of Gathering﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, on which He gathers the people of the heavens and the earth. ﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾. It is a form of tafā'ul from al-ghabn (loss), which is the forfeiting of a share. The one who is cheated (al-maghbūn) is the one who is deprived of his people and his dwellings in Paradise. On that day the loss of every disbeliever becomes apparent through his abandoning faith, and the loss of every believer through his shortcoming in doing good. ﴿And whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. The people of Madinah and Sham recited (qara'a) "nukaffir" and "nudkhilhu," and in Surat al-Talaq "nudkhilhu" with the nūn in all of these; the others recited with the yā'. ﴿Abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verses 10–14:

﴿Those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire, abiding therein. And evil is the destination.﴾

﴿No affliction befalls except by the permission of Allah﴾ [by His will and His decree] [[Addition from "B".]] ﴿And whoever believes in Allah﴾ and affirms that no affliction befalls him except by the permission of Allah, ﴿He will guide his heart﴾ He will grant him success in certainty, until he knows that what afflicted him would not have missed him, and what missed him would not have afflicted him, so he submits [to His decree] [[In "B": to the decree of Allah.]]. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾

﴿Allah - there is no deity except Him. And upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: These were men from the people of Makkah who embraced Islam and wished to emigrate (hijrah, migration) to Madinah, but their wives and children prevented them, and they said: "We were patient with your Islam, so we will not be patient with your separation from us." So they obeyed them and abandoned the emigration [[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi in Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah at-Taghabun: 9/222-223, and he said: "This is a sound hadith." Also at-Tabari: 28/124, and al-Hakim: 2/490, who said: "This hadith has a sound chain of narration, but they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." As-Suyuti in ad-Durr al-Manthur: 8/184 added its attribution to al-Firyabi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and at-Tabarani.]] [So Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿so beware of them﴾, that you obey them and leave off the emigration] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "A".]].

﴿But if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ This refers to one who remained with his family and children and did not emigrate. When he emigrated and saw that those who had preceded him in emigration had gained understanding of the religion, he intended to punish his wife and children who had held him back from emigration; and if they joined him in the land of emigration, he would not spend on them nor show them any good. So Allah, the Exalted, commanded them to pardon them and overlook [their conduct].

And 'Ata' ibn Yasar said: It was revealed concerning 'Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i. He had a family and children, and whenever he wished to go on a military campaign (ghazw), they wept before him and softened his heart, saying: "To whom will you leave us?" So he would be moved for them and remain [[Narrated by at-Tabari: 28/125.]]. Then Allah revealed: "Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you," because they bring you to abandon obedience. So beware of them, lest you accept from them.

﴿But if you pardon and overlook and forgive﴾, then do not punish them for opposing you. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verse 15:

﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾: a test, an examination, and a distraction from the Hereafter, through which a person falls into grave sins, withholds what is owed, and takes what is forbidden. ﴿And with Allah is a great reward.﴾ Some of them said: When Allah mentioned enmity, He introduced "min" (some of) for partition (li-l-tab'id), saying, "Indeed, among your spouses and your children are enemies to you" (64:14), because not all of them are enemies [in the manuscript "b," "bi-a'da'ikum," "to your enemies"]. He did not mention "min" in His saying, "Your wealth and your children are only a trial," because they are never free of trial and of preoccupying the heart.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to say: Let none of you say, "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from trial," for none of you possesses wealth, family, or children without them containing a trial. Rather, let him say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from misleading trials" [al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur, 8/185, to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id, 7/220: "al-Tabarani narrated it, and its isnad is interrupted (munqati'), and it includes al-Mas'udi, who became confused (ikhtalata)"].

Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Muzaffari informed us: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Faqih informed us: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Faqih informed us: Ahmad ibn Bakr ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us: al-Husayn ibn Waqid informed us, from Abdullah ibn Buraydah, who said: I heard my father Abu Buraydah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delivering a sermon to us when al-Hasan and al-Husayn came, wearing two red shirts, walking and stumbling. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came down from the pulpit, carried them, placed them before himself, and then said: "Allah has spoken the truth: 'Indeed, your wealth and your children are a trial' (64:15). I looked at these two boys walking and stumbling, and I could not be patient until I interrupted my speech and lifted them up" [Abu Dawud, in Prayer, chapter "The imam may interrupt the sermon for a matter that arises," 2/20; al-Tirmidhi, in Virtues, 10/278-279, and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith; we only know it from the narration of al-Husayn ibn Waqid"; al-Nasa'i, in Friday, chapter "The imam descending from the pulpit before finishing the sermon, interrupting his speech and returning to it on Friday," 3/108; Ibn Majah, in Clothing, chapter "Men wearing red," no. 2600, 2/1190; Ibn Hibban, no. 2230, p. 552; al-Hakim, 1/287; and Imam Ahmad, 5/354. al-Albani authenticated it in Sahih al-Jami', no. 3757].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verses 16–18:

﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾. "As much as you are able" (ما اسْتَطَعْتُمْ) — this verse abrogates (naskh) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Fear Allah with the fear that is due to Him﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 102]. ﴿And listen and obey﴾ Allah and His Messenger, ﴿and spend in charity; it is better for yourselves﴾: spend from your wealth, which is better for yourselves.

﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul﴾, meaning until he gives the right of Allah from his wealth, ﴿those are the successful﴾.
